ownership: Private; Bestseller (Anders Holch Povlsen) 71.29%, founders minority
sells: Discount beauty, personal care, household and snacks; 1,000+ stores in Denmark, Norway, Sweden, Netherlands, France, Finland, Portugal, Spain, Italy, Austria, Ireland (Romania from 2026)
fit_detail: NL, ES, IT, AT, FR etc. = 3+ F1 markets; young mass-market discount shoppers, not affluent; no performance/technology story; discount retail not crowded
flags: lapsed F1 tie via controlling parent: Bestseller's Jack & Jones sponsored Haas F1 (2018-19) and Kevin Magnussen - confirm before outreach
verdict_reason: Passes filters (revenue EUR ~1.6B FY2024); separately marketed brand of Bestseller (71%); parent's lapsed Haas/Magnussen sponsorship caps at Stretch.
best_angle: Fast pan-European roll-out (Romania 2026) needs brand awareness, and Bestseller already knows F1 from the Jack & Jones-Haas deal.

ownership: Public-sector owned: north-eastern Swiss cantons and cantonal utilities (100%)
sells: Hydro/nuclear/renewable power generation, grids, and pan-European energy trading and origination (30+ countries)
fit_detail: Trades/originates in many F1 markets (DE, IT, ES, US etc.); senior B2B energy buyers; renewables story moderate; power utility not on crowded list
verdict_reason: Passes filters (total income CHF 7.4B FY2024/25); no F1 tie found; reservation: publicly owned utility with weak brand-marketing motive.

ownership: Public (Nasdaq Stockholm: ARJO B); Getinge founding family (Stefan Persson-linked Carl Bennet AB) largest holder
sells: Patient-handling, hygiene, pressure-injury prevention and medical beds to hospitals and care homes; 100+ countries
fit_detail: Global sales incl. F1 markets; buyers are hospital procurement, not affluent 25-54; care story not performance; medtech not crowded
flags: B2B hospital equipment, no consumer angle
scale via revenue route (market cap < USD 1B)
verdict_reason: Passes scale via revenue (SEK ~11B FY2025); no F1 tie found; B2B hospital equipment with no consumer brand ambition.

ownership: Private; co-founders Vyacheslav Klymov and Volodymyr Popereshniuk
sells: Parcel delivery, logistics, fintech (NovaPay) in Ukraine plus Nova Post Europe in 16 countries (Poland, Moldova, Germany, Spain etc.)
fit_detail: Operates in Spain, Italy, Germany etc. (3+ F1 markets) but mostly Ukraine; mass consumers; tech-led growth and global-ambition story yes; logistics crowded on grid = 0
flags: market expansion: Ukraine -> 16 European countries; China and Canada planned 2026
verdict_reason: Passes filters (revenue USD ~1.36B 2024); no F1 tie found; reservation: logistics crowded on grid and core business in a war zone.
best_angle: Nova Post is expanding across Europe and into Canada/China and needs brand recognition beyond the Ukrainian diaspora.

ownership: Public (Euronext Paris: BON); controlled by Bonduelle family
sells: Canned, frozen and fresh-processed vegetables; Europe, Eurasia (incl. Russia), North America
valuation: Market cap well below USD 1B (2026, est)
fit_detail: Europe/North America = 3+ F1 markets; mass-market shoppers; no performance story; food not crowded
flags: significant Russia operations (Eurasia segment) - reputational check
verdict_reason: Passes filters (revenue EUR 2.19B FY2025-26); no F1 tie found; reservation: weak F1 story and Russia exposure.

ownership: Public (NSE: TATACHEM); Tata Sons and Tata group cos ~38% (not >50%)
sells: Soda ash, sodium bicarbonate, salt (Tata Salt sold via Tata Consumer), specialty chemicals; India, US, UK, Kenya
fit_detail: India, US, UK = 3+ F1 markets; industrial B2B buyers; commodity chemicals, no performance story; chemicals not crowded
flags: sister F1 tie: Tata Communications (Tata Sons sister co) F1 connectivity partner 2012-2020, broadcast connectivity partner from 2022 - not controlled entity
FY26 net loss INR 1,715 crore on US goodwill impairment
verdict_reason: Passes filters (market cap ~USD 2B est, 2026); no direct F1 tie (Tata Sons not >50% parent); commodity B2B chemicals with fit 1 and no brand ambition.

ownership: Public (Euronext Paris: MDM); lenders Alteri Investors / Eicos Investment Group taking control via restructuring
sells: Home decor and furniture; ~338 stores in France, Italy, Spain, Germany, Belgium etc. plus online
latest_raise: n/a; debt restructuring cutting bank debt 84% (conciliation protocol 18 Jun 2026)
fit_detail: France, Italy, Spain = 3+ F1 markets; aspirational 25-54 homeowners; no performance story; home decor not crowded
flags: financial restructuring after covenant breaches (conciliation Jun 2026)
verdict_reason: Fails hard filter 3 (distress): covenant breaches and financial restructuring/conciliation with Alteri/Eicos (Jun 2026), net loss EUR 406M FY2025. No F1 tie found.

sells: Lighting (Acuity Brands Lighting) and Intelligent Spaces (Distech building controls, QSC audio-visual); mainly North America, some Europe
fit_detail: US/Canada/Mexico plus Europe via Distech/QSC (3+ F1 markets, NA-heavy); senior B2B buyers (facilities, architects); intelligent-spaces technology story; lighting not crowded
verdict_reason: Passes filters (revenue USD 4.3B FY2025; market cap ~USD 9.8B est); no F1 tie found; reservation: North America-centric B2B.
best_angle: Recently rebranded Acuity Inc. could showcase smart-building/venue tech (QSC audio, Distech) at US Grands Prix where F1 is growing fastest.

ownership: Private; KKCG (Karel Komarek) since 2024; previously Oaktree/Cornerstone (2019-24)
sells: Software engineering, digital transformation and IT consulting for pharma, finance, insurance, automotive; Europe and US
valuation: Deal value 'several billion CZK' (2024, e15 report, est)
fit_detail: Germany, Poland, US, Switzerland = 3+ F1 markets; senior B2B tech buyers; engineering/technology story; IT services not crowded
flags: to be combined with KKCG's Qinshift IT unit
verdict_reason: Passes scale only via USD 150-500M revenue route (est, unverified); no F1 tie found for Avenga or KKCG/Allwyn; capped at Stretch.

ownership: Public (TASE: DELG); Isaac Dabah family largest holder
sells: Intimate apparel, socks, activewear, denim/leisure: own brands (Delta, Schiesser, Splendid, PJ Salvage) plus licences (adidas, Calvin Klein, Tommy Hilfiger, Columbia) and private label; US, Europe, Israel
fit_detail: US, Germany, UK, Israel = 3+ F1 markets; mass-market shoppers; no performance story; apparel not crowded
flags: licensor adidas is an F1 team partner (not a Delta Galil tie)
verdict_reason: Passes filters (revenue USD 2.12B FY2025); no F1 tie found; mainly private-label/licensed manufacturing with limited own-brand ambition.
